title: Working Out the Paydown Called for before a Spending Restriction Comes Off
content:
The paydown an employee is asked to pay onto their own Employee Meal Account before a spending restriction can be taken off is worked out from the charges the account carries and from the value already standing on it.

## 1. The measured balance

The measured balance is every charge accrued on the account to date less every recovery remitted on it to date, and it is never read as less than nothing.

## 2. The required share

The required share is the reinstatement share printed against the meal plan the account is held on.

## 3. The gross paydown

The gross paydown is the measured balance taken at the required share and rounded to two decimal places at that step.

## 4. Stored value already on the account

None of the stored value already standing on the account is credited against the gross paydown.

## 5. A working balance at the till

Nothing is added to the paydown to restore a working balance at the till.

## 6. Guest meals

Nothing is added to the paydown for guest meals.

## 7. Assembling the figure

The paydown is worked out in this order and in no other: the credit for stored value is taken off the gross paydown first, and that remainder, never read as less than nothing, has the amount added to restore a working balance and the amount added for guest meals put on top of it; the figure is then raised to the smallest single load the plan accepts if it falls below it, and finally held to the largest single load the plan accepts. The figure is rounded to two decimal places at the end, over and above the two roundings named above.

## 8. Who pays it

The employee makes this payment in person from a card they hold, since it is their own money.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

Suppose the account's ledger shows charges accrued to date of $410.00 and recoveries remitted to date of $130.00, and that the plan it is held on prints, for this illustration, a reinstatement share of 40 percent, a smallest single load of $8.00 and a largest single load of $200.00.

The measured balance is $410.00 less $130.00, or $280.00. The required share is 40 percent, so the gross paydown is $280.00 taken at 40 percent, which is $112.00, rounded at that step. Nothing is credited for stored value, so $112.00 stands; nothing is added to restore a working balance and nothing for guest meals, so it stands still; $112.00 is above the smallest single load of $8.00 and below the largest of $200.00, so neither the raising nor the holding moves it. Rounded once more at the end, the paydown called for is $112.00.

Had the same measured balance produced a gross paydown of $6.40 against a smallest single load of $8.00, the raising step would take the figure to $8.00; had it produced $260.00 against a largest single load of $200.00, the holding step would take it to $200.00.


## How a window of calendar months is counted

A window of calendar months in this policy runs back from the day the account is worked and never from the turn of a named month: an entry falls inside such a window while fewer than that many whole months have gone by since the day it was booked, a whole month going by only when the same day of the month comes round again, so an entry exactly that many whole months old falls outside it, and an entry booked after the day the account is worked falls outside it too.
